title: Amarante à la queue de bœuf (Folong or Endeng with Oxtail)
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik.com)
desc: Steamed amaranth leaves, pressure-cooked oxtail with aromatics, and a tomato stew reduced uncovered — the dish the page says is known as endeng or folong in Central Africa.
longDesc: Afrik’s recipe for amaranth with oxtail: the leaves are steamed in a couscoussier, the oxtail is pressure-cooked with the aromatics, the leaves are chopped, stewed with tomato, and the sauce reduced uncovered. The page does not give times. The leaves are known as endeng or folong in Central Africa, with Gabon, Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea named.
ingredients: Pepper and salt — amounts not printed
steps: Steam the amaranth leaves in a couscoussier.
Pressure-cook the oxtail with the aromatics until tender.
Stew the leaves with the tomato, adding the oxtail.
chefTips: The only printed cues are ‘une fois tendre’ for the oxtail and a reduced sauce.
No times are printed — judge by tenderness.
Wash the leaves well before steaming.
commonMistakes: Leaving the sauce thin instead of reducing it.
healthBenefits: Amaranth leaves add iron-rich greens; oxtail adds protein and fat.
culturalNote: The page names the leaf endeng or folong in Central Africa and mentions Gabon, Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea; no community is named.
